definition: The principle of collecting, processing, and storing only the minimum amount of personal data necessary to achieve a specific, legitimate purpose.
metaDescription: Data minimization is a privacy principle requiring organizations to collect only necessary personal data. Learn why it matters for privacy protection.
simpleExplanation: Data minimization means companies should only ask for and keep the personal information they actually need. If a pizza delivery app only needs your address and phone number, it shouldn't also collect your birthday, job title, or social media profiles.
whyItMatters: The less personal data collected and stored, the lower the risk of privacy breaches, identity theft, and misuse. It reduces your digital footprint and limits how much companies know about you, giving you better control over your personal information.
technicalDetail: Data minimization involves implementing collection limits at the point of data entry, setting automatic deletion schedules for unnecessary data, conducting regular data audits, and designing systems that operate with minimal data requirements. This principle is often enforced through privacy-by-design architectures and data governance policies.

examples.explanation: An e-commerce site only collects your name, shipping address, and payment method for purchases, rather than also requesting your age, income, marital status, or browsing history from other sites.
A newsletter signup form only asks for your email address instead of also requiring your full name, phone number, company, and postal address when those aren't needed to send emails.
A weather app only accesses your general location to show local forecasts, rather than continuously tracking your precise GPS coordinates and storing your movement history.
